records.name: VC Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the Video Consortium, a network for nonfiction filmmakers. Each month it holds an in person gathering, such as a screening, panel, workshop or social evening.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly gathering to meet other nonfiction filmmakers and hear about jobs and resources. Members also get a jobs board, a directory profile and a weekly newsletter.

schedule.text: Monthly in person gatherings around Philadelphia, with screenings, panels, workshops and social evenings.

cost.text: Essential membership is free with a one time $10 application fee. Gold membership is $119 a year or $12.50 a month, and an annual Gold plan waives the application fee. Gold members attend gatherings free. The site does not give a price for other attendees. Students get half off the fees.

first_step.how: If you work or study in nonfiction video, apply for an Essential membership at videoconsortium.org/join. The $10 fee is one time, and applications are reviewed in about 2 to 5 business days.
first_step.basis: Joining needs an application that is reviewed before you are a member, and eligibility is limited to people working or studying in nonfiction video. The site does not say whether a non-member can attend a gathering.
first_step.what_to_expect: Gatherings are monthly, in person and social, with screenings, panels and workshops. The site does not say how long a gathering lasts. Members meet other nonfiction filmmakers and hear about jobs.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for the date, time and venue before you go.
Apply well before a gathering, since reviews take about 2 to 5 business days.

records.notes: Tier 1 Wednesday evening pattern dropped: it came from a single dated gathering, and the site does not state a repeat day. Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because membership needs an application. Gathering length is not stated.

records.name: Volunteer at a prison
records.summary: Trains volunteers to provide educational and spiritual support to people held at one of four Philadelphia Department of Prisons facilities.
records.what_you_do: Give educational or spiritual support to people held in one of the four city facilities, after finishing 16 hours of training and a background check.

locations.label: One of four Philadelphia Department of Prisons facilities: Curran-Fromhold, the Detention Center, Philadelphia Industrial Correctional Center, or Riverside

first_step.how: Email the volunteer application to pdp.volunteer@prisons.phila.gov. The form is on the City's form page at phila.gov/documents/philadelphia-prisons-volunteer-form/.
first_step.basis: Applicants must be approved by the Volunteer Services Division, then complete 16 hours of training and a background check before they start. Applications that do not fit a program need are turned down.
first_step.what_to_expect: Accepted volunteers first finish 16 hours of training at the Department of Prisons training academy, and the academy contacts them to start the background check. After that, volunteers give educational or spiritual support inside a facility. The page does not describe what a first visit looks like.
first_visit_tips: Check the rules before you apply: volunteers must be 21 or older with a valid state ID, and people who were incarcerated must wait six months after release.
Relatives of people held in the system must say so on the application and are not placed at the same facility.
Questions go to 215-685-8149. Religious volunteer questions go to 215-685-8385.

records.notes: Tier 1 had last sign of life 2025-04. The form page shows a March 28, 2025 release date, so 2025-03 is used; the 2025-04 date could not be reproduced. The pages checked do not list the clearance checks by name, so none are listed. Court-ordered hours and service hours letters are not mentioned on any page checked. Facility street addresses are not published.

records.name: Vox Populi Gallery
records.summary: An artist-run gallery in North Chinatown that hosts exhibitions, performances, film screenings, and community events, and runs open calls and space rentals for artists.
records.what_you_do: Visit during open hours or come to an exhibition opening, performance or screening. Artists can apply to open calls, and supporters can give monthly to the Vox Circle or join the board.

schedule.text: Open to the public on Thursdays from 4 to 6 pm and Fridays to Sundays from 12 to 6 pm, or by appointment. Exhibitions and events are listed on the website.

cost.text: The site does not state an admission price for open hours. Some events have tickets. Optional Vox Circle giving starts at $5 a month.

access.notes: Five steps from the street to the first floor landing, where the passenger elevator starts. The elevator door is 29 inches wide and may not fit every wheelchair or motorized chair. The third floor has no further steps. Ramp access is available if you contact the gallery ahead. Personal care attendants and service animals are welcome. The restroom door is 34 inches wide and has grab bars; the page does not say whether the restroom is step free.

first_step.how: Visit during open hours: Thursdays from 4 to 6 pm, or Fridays to Sundays from 12 to 6 pm. You can also join the mailing list on the website.
first_step.basis: Open to the public on set days, with a clear events calendar and a mailing list. No beginner program or volunteer program is listed on the pages checked.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open hours let you see the current exhibitions in the third floor gallery. The site does not state an admission charge for open hours. Performances and screenings are separate events with their own times, and some are ticketed.
first_visit_tips: If you need a ramp, call 215-238-1236 or email events@voxpopuligallery.org before you come.
Check the events page for performances and screenings, which have their own times and tickets.
Gallery spaces use window air conditioners, not central air.

records.notes: Hours come from the visit page. Open calls (the $99 exhibition and the fall exhibition call) have deadlines on news posts that were not read, so no deadlines are recorded. Board and internship openings are listed under Opportunities and were not checked. Vox Circle is optional monthly giving; it is not needed to visit.

records.name: Washington Square West Civic Association
records.summary: The neighborhood civic association for Washington Square West. It describes itself as Philadelphia's first civic association, runs community gardens, and co-hosts Love Your Park garden days with Farm Philly.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly board meeting, which is open to the public, or help at a Love Your Park garden day. Membership joins and renewals are handled online.

schedule.text: Board of Directors meetings are held the second Tuesday of each month at 7 pm and are open to the public. The meeting place is not listed on the site.

cost.text: The membership page does not list dues. Joining and renewing happen through an online portal.

first_step.how: Attend the second Tuesday board meeting at 7 pm. The meeting place is not on the site, so confirm it through the contact page or by phone before you go.
first_step.basis: Board meetings are public, and membership joins online. The meeting place is not on the site, so the first visit takes one call or email to confirm.
first_step.what_to_expect: The board meeting is a public monthly meeting held on the second Tuesday at 7 pm. The site does not describe the agenda or how long the meeting runs. Garden days are a hands on way to meet the association's volunteers.
first_visit_tips: Call 267-603-1318 or email info@washwestcivic.org to confirm the meeting place. The office phone is voicemail only.
Membership joins and renewals are done through the online portal linked on the membership page.
Ask about garden days, which the association co-hosts with Farm Philly.

records.notes: Tier 1 schedule (the May 9 garden day, a dated event) replaced with the monthly board meeting from the association's meetings page. The group's own site shows news only from December 2022 to January 2023 and an empty calendar, so active status rests on the May 2026 Love Your Park listing and the spring 2026 waitlist entries on the association's garden page. Email and phone come from the group's own pages; tier 1 used zoning@ and 215 806 0960 from the city registry, which are not sent. The office address (1100 Walnut MOB Room B113) is a mailing office, not a meeting place, so it is not listed as a location. Contact name comes from the city registry.

records.name: South Street Community Garden
records.summary: One of the Washington Square West Civic Association's community gardens, at 839 South St. Membership is for people whose primary home is in the neighborhood, and the waitlist can be long.
records.what_you_do: Garden members follow the association's garden rules. The public can see the garden on the association's open garden days.

first_step.how: If your primary home is in Washington Square West, apply for garden membership through the association's waitlist page at washwestcivic.org/community-gardens/waitlist, choosing a first and second garden. Otherwise, come to a public open garden day if one is announced.
first_step.basis: Members must have a primary home in Washington Square West, and the waitlist page says some members wait three years for a plot.
first_step.what_to_expect: The association has held public Open Garden Days at this garden, including one in May 2026 during Love Your Park Week. Membership requires following the garden rules and having a primary home in the neighborhood. The garden page does not describe a typical visit or work day.
first_visit_tips: When you apply, you pick a first and second choice garden, and you are added to both waitlists.
The garden page mentions the garden rules but does not link them, so ask the association for a copy.

records.notes: Tier 1 treated this as a public Friends garden with no web page. The association's garden page shows membership is for Washington Square West residents, and the waitlist page says some members wait three years for a plot, so audience is residents, newcomer rating is 1, and kind changed from friends_group to garden. The tier 1 aliases Sartain Community Garden, Sartain Garden, Waverly Street Community Garden and Sartain Street Community Garden are not sent: the association page gives Sartain and Waverly separate addresses, so they look like other gardens. Sartain and Waverly are listed in leads_only. The garden rules are mentioned but not linked.

records.name: We Are the Seeds
records.summary: A Native-led group in Philadelphia that shares and teaches Indigenous arts and cultures. It runs a yearly Seeds Philly weekend, a podcast, and an Indigenous listening garden in West Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Go to the Seeds Philly weekend, listen to the podcast, or ask the group to bring a workshop to your school or organization. The listening garden has no published street address or hours.

schedule.text: Seeds Philly is a yearly weekend of arts, talks and workshops. The listening garden has no posted hours.

locations.label: Indigenous listening garden, West Philadelphia (street address not published)

cost.text: The group's site does not give a price for its programs. It takes donations through a fundraising page.

first_step.how: Watch the group's site for the next Seeds Philly weekend, or use the site's request form to ask for a workshop for your school or group.
first_step.basis: The festival is open to the public, and the site explains how schools and groups can request a workshop. No volunteer roles or beginner program are listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Seeds Philly is a two-day weekend with talks, live art, short films, workshops and an Indigenous art show. The 2026 weekend was pay what you can, with a $20 suggested donation. A September 2026 Inquirer report said organizers may not hold the festival again for the foreseeable future, because the money has run out.
first_visit_tips: Check with the group before you plan a trip, since the festival's future is uncertain.
The garden's street address and hours are not published, so ask the group before visiting.
Follow the group on Instagram or its Substack for updates.

records.notes: The group's /gardens page returned HTTP 404 (not a block), and one web search found no address or hours for the listening garden. The Inquirer report (Sept 19, 2026) says the group runs listening gardens in West and North Philadelphia and in Kensington; the group's own page names one in West Philadelphia, so the record keeps that. The report's statement that the festival may not return is a news report, not a group statement, and is recorded as one. Tier 1 cited a CultureWorks fiscal sponsorship page; the group's home page names CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia as the organization it is a project of. Neither parent organization has a URL seen on the pages read, so neither is listed as a lead. A search result described a May 30, 2026 Root Song workshop at Bartram's Garden co-led with the group; it was not fetched and is not recorded.

records.name: We Walk PHL
records.summary: A free walking group that meets in public parks across Philadelphia. Trained local leaders guide about an hour of walking, one to three times a week depending on the park. The program is supported by Parks and Recreation, the Fairmount Park Conservancy and the Department of Public Health.
records.what_you_do: Walk with neighbors for about an hour in a park near you, and get to know people who walk the same route.

schedule.text: Walks last about an hour, one to three a week depending on the park. The fall season runs September 1 to October 31. The Bartram's Garden walk meets every Thursday from 5 to 6 pm.

locations.label: Public parks across Philadelphia (varies by walk)

first_step.how: Find the walk nearest you on the We Walk PHL registration page on GivePulse, or call 215-309-5523. The Bartram's Garden walk meets on Thursdays from 5 to 6 pm at the Welcome Center.
first_step.basis: Free and open to the public, with a registration portal and a phone line. The pages do not say whether first time walkers get any extra help, and they do not say whether registration is needed before the first walk.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each walk lasts about an hour and is guided by a trained local leader. The pages do not describe the pace or distance, so ask the program before you go. Walks are free.
first_visit_tips: At Bartram's Garden, walk leaders greet people at the start, so go to the Welcome Center at 5400 Lindbergh Boulevard.
Ask the program about pace and distance if you want an easier walk.
Check the park and time before each walk, since the schedule varies by park.

records.notes: Tier 1 last sign of life of 2026-09 was not supported by the Schuylkill Banks listing, which covers Thursday walks from May 1 to June 25; the dated Bartram's Garden event (June 18, 2026) is used instead. The Thursday 5 to 6 pm pattern comes from the Bartram's Garden listing; other parks are not confirmed. A later Bartram's Garden tile runs through October 29 but shows no year, so it is not used. The City page is dated September 10, 2025 and gives the fall season without a year. Newcomer rating is 3, not 4: a Love Your Park Week 2026 summary quoted 'newcomers are always welcome', which would support a 4 if the wording is confirmed on that page.

leads_only.note: Listed on the Washington Square West Civic Association garden page as a separate garden at 1114 to 1118 Locust St. No separate website seen. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Waverly Garden
leads_only.note: Listed on the Washington Square West Civic Association garden page as a separate garden at 1127 to 1131 Waverly St. No separate website seen. Not checked.

notes: Run summary: seven groups, all written as publish. Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used; 23 WebFetch used of 60. No rate limiting or bot checks seen. wearetheseeds.org/gardens returned HTTP 404 (not a block). Leads dropped with reasons (no fetch): Farm Philly (named on the Love Your Park page, no URL seen); CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia (named as parent on the We Are the Seeds home page, no URL seen); CAO Collective and Dusky Projects (named on the Vox Populi site, no URLs seen); Fairmount Park Conservancy (named as a We Walk PHL supporter, no URL seen); Bartram's Garden (has its own site, but it is the venue for one We Walk PHL walk, and that walk is recorded under We Walk PHL; not fetched). Corrections to tier 1: volunteer-at-a-prison now shows a background check; vox-populi-gallery now has hours, step-free detail and the Thursday and weekend schedule; washington-square-west-civic-association now has the monthly board meeting as its schedule, and its phone and email now come from its own pages; waverly-street-community-garden is a residents-only garden with a long waitlist, not a public Friends garden; we-walk-phl last sign of life moved from 2026-09 to 2026-06. Unverified or left out: Vox open-call deadlines (news posts not read); Seeds garden address and hours (none found); We Walk PHL days and times beyond the Bartram's Garden walk.
